terra.problem: Ezekiel living in Babylon is a fact from outside this passage and needs its own reference.
The report that the city was taken does not establish that there was no peace treaty.
The passage does not say the walls failed or describe a walk to Ezekiel’s door. Marking the walk as a guess does not make up for adding those events.
The text places the LORD’s hand upon Ezekiel in the evening, but says only that his mouth was opened before the man arrived in the morning.
The passage does not say Ezekiel’s eyes were fine the whole time.
Saying it happened in the evening places the opening of Ezekiel’s mouth at a time the text does not specify.
The news was that the city had been taken. It did not mention the walls.
Papa comments on how he will tell the passage: “I’ll just say it plainly.”
Ezekiel living in Babylon needs a reference outside this passage. Papa also comments on how he tells the passage: “I’ll leave it plain.”
“No joke here” comments on how Papa tells the passage.
The invitation to hear the message does not establish that nobody was running from Ezekiel.
The cookie-box comparison does not match the contrast. A box marked homemade being empty does not convey expressing love while pursuing dishonest gain.
The passage compares Ezekiel to a singer, but does not state as a fact that the people enjoy listening.
